questions.stem: In what form does IaaS provide compute power and storage to customers?
questions.explanation: In IaaS, online compute power and storage are provided to customers in the shape of Virtual Machines.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for installing and upgrading software in an IaaS arrangement?
options: Nobody, as software is not used in IaaS
questions.explanation: Customers must bring their own software, tools and IT solutions and manage the environment themselves, including installing and upgrading software.

questions.stem: How does a cloud service provider charge for IaaS?
options: Based on compute and storage usage
questions.explanation: The cloud service provider charges based on compute and storage usage.

questions.stem: In the laptop analogy for IaaS from I Am Datapedia!, what does the service provider supply?
options: Laptops with only the operating system of your choice
Laptops with a pre-built solution ready to use
Only the data stored on the laptops
A single function running on the laptop
questions.explanation: In IaaS the provider buys the laptops (infrastructure) with ONLY the operating system of your choice and gives you access; everything else is your job.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the customer's responsibilities under IaaS?
options: Configuring Disaster Recovery and High Availability
Buying and hosting the physical servers
questions.explanation: Under IaaS the provider supplies the infrastructure; the customer handles security software, encryption, DR/HA, database installation and upgrades.

questions.stem: Which phrase summarises IaaS in a nutshell?
options: Pulling data on demand through APIs
Deploying only functions in the Cloud
Only having infrastructure with no support to maintain software
questions.explanation: 'In nutshell, only having Infrastructure with no support to maintain software(s) is IaaS.'

questions.stem: Under IaaS, who manages High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR)?
questions.explanation: Customers manage the environment on their own, including HA, DR, compute power and storage standards.

questions.stem: In the IaaS laptop analogy, what does keeping a second laptop and moving data to it periodically illustrate?
options: A Disaster Recovery and High Availability strategy
questions.explanation: Backing up to an external disk and keeping a second laptop in sync so work can continue if the first crashes represents the DR and HA strategy the customer must configure.

questions.stem: What must customers bring to an IaaS environment?
options: Their own software, tools and IT solutions
questions.explanation: Customers must bring their own software, tools and IT solutions and then manage the environment themselves.

questions.stem: Which of these is the ONLY thing pre-installed by the provider on an IaaS virtual machine in the analogy?
options: An operating system of your choice
questions.explanation: The provider supplies the infrastructure with only the operating system of your choice; databases, Office, security software and encryption are the customer's tasks.
